node.description: Historian of early America who made the relation between slavery and freedom a central interpretive problem. In his1972 address,Morgan rejects treating enslavement as an exception to the national story or freedom as mere disguise. His Virginia-centered argument asks how racial domination and the independence claimed by white colonists developed together. Its particular mechanism remains open to debate rather than explaining every colonial society.

proposed_edges.relationship: Morgan’s American paradox connects revolutionary commitments to independence with the simultaneous development of slaveholding society.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own1972 pp5–8 rejects both simple hypocrisy and a story that treats slavery as an exception; Virginia-centered mechanism is bounded.

proposed_edges.relationship: Morgan places racial domination within the formation of colonial freedom and social independence.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own1972 pp5–8 explicitly recognizes racism while asking about the material/social conditions of independence; not a universal account of every colony.
